As far as I know there are 3 ways to gain shield: - kami brew (potion) - fortress (gain at start of battle -2hp) -reactive shield (gain shield on damage) Kami brew being an instant to drink, and having the arbility to be safely stored in a potion slot until you are about to take damage means that making an always online shield with Shield retention basically functions like an extra potions slot that only works for Kami brew. Since Kami brew is the most consistently available way to recieve shield, Shield retention's purpose is kind of unneccicary, as its function regarding kami brew is already filled by the extra potion slot upgrade. Fortess straight up invalidates shield retention, as having it makes shield retention do nothing. Reactive shield is the most synergistic with Shield retention, some battles you might only take one hit, making your shield go to waste. This is a legitimately useful combo, however takes a lot of coinage and 2 perks from the same specific shop. My Idea: Make it so Shield retention, on top of its current effect, allows for 2 layers of shield, needing to be individually filled and depleted. this means that for defensive purposes, it becomes better than a potion slot for storing shield. While still not being an unconditional upside. It also gains a synergy with Fortress, now being able to, if you manage to go hitless for multiple stages, stack layers of shielding for "free". Finally it does not really gain extra synergy with Reactive shielding, however it already had good synergy with it, so it should be fine. This change would increase power, however I do think that in its current state it is quite weak Additionally, it could be in incremental powerup, allowing for additional layers every time it is picked up, however that could be too much. [2024/01/14 12:28] dragon_of_celts [1] **Getsugasan** Just a worse damage-upgraded spear, right? Well, it depends. Bad: If you're about to be hit by the target, they'll hit you before you kill them. Inconsequential: If there are no immediate threats to deal with, it makes no difference if you attack before the enemies act or after. Beneficial: If there are prepared enemies on the far side of the soon-to-be-killed target, it effectively gives you an extra turn to deal with them. So I was playing around with the Shogun's blaze attack (achieved by forcing it into my deck via RunSave moddification) and the fact it occurred *after* the enemies attack/move made actually for interesting strategies. I'd imagine it would be blue to compliment the red color of the free play effect. I will dub this effect "last play" to again go with the "free play" effect. I am interested in longer que combos and have a nuanced proposal of how to do that without breaking too much game and display: The least disruptive way is to allow free-play tiles to be played “before” any non-free play tile in the same que position. This could be shown by overlaying transparent free-play tiles over opaque non-free play tiles or by slotting them to the left of the que positions. The free play resolves first, then the non-free tile, for each position in the que. Free plays could still be played alone in the que position for extra flexibility. Their long cooldowns also reduce the impact of this change on player power. (Some combo skills may still need to be reworked.) Free-play abilities are supposed to be rare and powerful, but at present are best used to instantly move into a better position or bail out when a player isnt prepared for an attack. The tile combos also feel the least exciting when a free play tile is involved because it’s one less attack. Since the tiles arent attacks, they would be great candidates for making more complex combos without breaking the combo skills too hard. Imagine being able to move, hit, teleport, hit and hit with the help of two free play cards! Ordeal of the Cunning (2 waves) - Enchant a tile with Frostbite +2 CD, target is frozen and cursed. Once initiated, all enemy attacks freeze you for 1 turn. Game encourages stacking upgrades on 1 or 2 skills, so players naturally upgrade skills they get early (skills found late are usually sacrificed/not used) 2. Players are only offered one skill per biome and there are more weak/boring skills than fun/cool ones, so there aren't many chances to see the cool skills 3. Gold is better spent on buying/rerolling upgrades than on rerolling for skills 4. It feels like there's a rarity system for skills such that fun and cool skills appear less often, especially early on Because of this, most of my runs are very similar, where I focus on upgrading my starting skill plus whatever skill I picked up early (usually a weak/boring skill) It's such a shame since many of the later skills are really cool but I never properly use them My suggestions to improve this situation: 1. Increase number of skill choices to 3, more player choice = more agency on our builds = more fun 2. Sell skills on shops (except for Sacrifice shops) 3. Using the teleport tile will then swap you with anything that happens to have moved on that space, but would remove the marked spot. Namewise, Warp would be the most succinct. Example: > Warp > Base Cooldown - 5~6 > Mark the spot you are currently standing on. The tile will change to Return. > > Return > Base Cooldown - 5~6 > Return to and remove the spot you marked with Warp, swapping positions with a target if it's on the mark. However, since the Warden and the Shielder are not compatible with just 2 traits, and therefore can not be elite, the Avenger would most likely be unable to be elite. Lore: She is based off of the south-Asian trope of a ghost woman in a white dress, twisted feet and long dark her in front of her who was done wrong by some corrupt people. There are many different interpretations of what this ghost lady is, though in this scenario, the Avenger was a usual woman, who after the scarring and blah blah blah, got killed by the Shogun as he grew more furious, which made her think that almost all humans are evil. Yumi Sniper's Volley, but push or pull the target toward or away from the caster, respectively. The damage of each starts at 1, and increases by 1 with every miss, but resets when a target (intended or not) is hit. They may also cause collision damage from the push or pull. Kappa prefer to remain behind other enemies, and will use Mirror (and movement) to affect such, if possible. If Mirror is queued and the destination side of the board will no longer hide them, they will not remove it from their queue, but will not execute it without also queuing an attack. If there are no enemies between Kappa (or Kappa's destination, if Mirror is equipped) and player, and they cannot move behind an enemy with Mirror (and movement), Kappa will use Torrential Push to try to keep player away (and maybe collide with an enemy on the far side from the player). If there is an enemy between Kappa and player, he will use Torrential Pull to try to make player collide with an enemy between him and the player. Special passive attribute: Every time a tile damages (or vanquishes) Kappa, its cool down increases by 1 (for the remainder of the area; will revert to normal upon leaving the area). No effect on tiles with max cool down. This enemy is: **Nukekubi** *Do not get startled or scared by this seemingly dead body, for its true spirit will attack you if you let your guard down.* **HP**: 4, **Trait(s)**: None, **Tiles**: Summon, Chakram *(With 1 base damage)* Behavior: Nukekubi goes for Summon, summoning a **Nukekubi Head** (look below). After summoning the head, she goes for Chakram, which already has 1 base attack, and will increase in power if her allies get killed as long as it is in the queue. [2024/11/18 2:45] starfoxshooter New region: The Mirror Lands *Forever changing and unpredictable, the Mirror Lands have doomed many adventurers and trapped many more...* The Mirror Lands are a 3rd option to the spirit gateway and forsaken grounds, that can only be reached by using the rain of mirrors item after beating the moonlit port. Main gimmick: Certain enemies can move you and themselves around the board, using tiles like Mirror and Origin of symmetry, tiles that use the tile on you(so for example: a mirror that an enemy uses and targets you) as well as the tile Skill Copy (see below). Skill Copy: the enemy copies your special move(swap, push, e.t.c) and can use it against you Boss 1: The Figure *Legends say The Figure is a manifestation of deceased adventurers, who once were lost to the Mirror Land's. Some say you can still hear their cry's of anguish in the night if you listen closely..* Traits: Quick, Unpoisonable Behavior: Stays near the center of the board, occasionally summoning enemies, and uses a combination of movement tiles on you to keep you at bay, occasionally moving you next to them or, them moving next to you and to use offensive tiles like swirl Boss 1 Gimmick: similar to Sato, the screen will eventually fade to black,, before the board comes back and everything is the same, except for The Figure, which randomly selects one of the five playable characters and gains their special move as well as their base tile set to use against you. Reward: Similar to the Moonlit Port, you will get a special shop at the end of the section, which ofc sells skills but also sells an exclusive enchant called Mirror. Enchant: Mirror: all tiles that are one directional (Katana, Kunai, e.t.c) become bidirectional and hit both sides of you similar to how swirl works. Also adds +3 cooldown. Ok that's it thx for reading (sry for the multiple paragraphs lol) let me know what you think and what you would change if you don't like it! He uses it randomly after around 3-4 attacks, which switches him to his next phase (Dog -> Cat -> Rabbit -> Dog -> etc.). His Cat mode focuses on ranged attacks: Arrow, Kunai, Shadow dash then Twin Tessen, Ki push (Only if player is too close). Rabbit Mode: Double Summon, Smoke Bomb, Mirror, Volley. The idea of the boss is to constantly switch up his fighting style to counter all player decks. Hookblade and Dragon punch in Dog mode are also only used if a enemy is left from the rabbit mode, and infront of Tsunayoshi.
